recipes.name: Coq au Vin
ingredients: For the Coq au Vin Sauce
1 cup water, cold or warm temperature
instructions: For the Prep
For the Chicken Prep
Trim excess skin from the chicken thighs, then transfer to a rimmed baking sheet and thoroughly dry brine with kosher salt. - 4 (1 1/2 lbs) chicken thighs or drumsticks - kosher salt
Then, transfer to the fridge uncovered for at least 6 hours to ideally 24 hours, or up 36 hours. - For the Chicken
After at least 6 hours, the skin should be dry and more translucent with a tacky, semi-sticky texture. - For the Chicken
Set aside while you prepare the remaining ingredients. - For the Chicken
For the Bacon Prep
Cut bacon slabs into bite-sized pieces. - ½ lb butcher cut bacon
Then, transfer to a cold nonstick pan, spreading the pieces out into an even layer. - ½ lb butcher cut bacon
Add water to the pan. Then, cook over medium heat and cover with a lid for 5 minutes or until the fat begins to render out. - ¼ cup water - ½ lb butcher cut bacon
Remove the lid and allow the water to evaporate. - For the Bacon
Maintain the medium heat and cook the bacon for 5-7 minutes, stirring frequently until all the fat has rendered out, and the bacon is browned and crunchy. - For the Bacon
When the bacon is finished cooking, strain the rendered fat through a fine mesh sieve, reserving for later use. - For the Bacon
Spread the cooked bacon out on a paper towel-lined plate and allow to cool. - For the Bacon
Meanwhile, prepare the vegetables.
For the Vegetables Prep
Chop the yellow onion, celery, and parsnip into uniform pieces. - 1 yellow onion - 2 celery stalks - 1 parsnip
Then, thinly slice the garlic lengthwise. - 3 big garlic cloves
Set aside.
For the Bouquet Garni

Add all herbs, mushrooms, and peppercorns to the cheesecloth and tie it off into a little bundle. Set aside. - 3 stems parsley - 3 stems thyme - 1 stem rosemary - 3 ½ bay leaves - 4 dried porcini mushrooms - 1 tsp peppercorns
For the Sauce Prep
Prepare red wine in a measuring cup. - 1 ½ cup full bodied red wine
Combine Better than Bouillon in a bowl with cold or room temp water. - 1 tsp Better than Bouillon - 1 cup water cold or warm temperature
Then, bloom the gelatin, sprinkling over top slowly, a little bit at a time. Let the stock sit to allow proper hydration. - (2 1/2 tsp) unflavored gelatin
For the Cooking
For the Chicken
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Transfer the dry-brined chicken thighs skin-side down to a cold stainless steel pan on a large burner for solid, even heat. - For the Chicken
Turn heat to medium low and when about ¼ cup of fat has rendered out, increase the heat to medium, tilting the pan to ensure the chicken edges are fried by the fat. - For the Chicken
The chicken thighs skin is fried when they lift easily from the bottom of the pan with no resistance. - For the Chicken
Transfer the chicken thighs to a plate, reserving about 2 tbsp of the chicken fat in the pan. - For the Chicken - reserved chicken fat
Then, add 2 tablespoons bacon fat to the pan. - reserved bacon fat

Over medium-high heat, add the vegetables and sauté the vegetables until they begin to release moisture, then scrape the fond up from the bottom of the pan. - 2 large carrots peeled - 2 celery stalks - 1 yellow onion - 1 parsnip

When the vegetables start to color and caramelize, quickly add the slivered garlic, flour, and tomato paste, sautéeing for 30 seconds between each addition. - 3 big garlic cloves - 1 tbsp flour - 2 tbsp tomato paste
When the tomato paste starts to stick to the bottom of the pan, scrape it up, kill the heat, then add a splash of brandy, using a stick lighter to carefully flambé. - brandy optional

Once the brandy has burned off, allow the remaining liquid to evaporate, then scrape the fond from the bottom of the pan. Add bloomed chicken stock. - 1 tsp Better than Bouillon - 1 cup water cold or warm temperature - (2 1/2 tsp) unflavored gelatin
Then, add red wine, stirring to combine. - full bodied red wine

Bring to a simmer then add Bouquet Garni. Turn off the heat then add the chicken thighs back to the pan, making sure the skin is above the water level. - Bouquet Garni - (1 1/2 lbs) chicken thighs or drumsticks - For the Chicken - For the Coq au Vin Sauce

Transfer the entire pan to the preheated oven for 45 to 1 hour until the chicken is tender, the vegetables are fully cooked, and the chicken skin is crispy. - For the Chicken - For the Vegetables - For the Bouquet Garni - For the Coq au Vin Sauce
For the Mushrooms
Add melted butter to a nonstick pan over medium heat and melt until foamy. - 1 ½ tbsp salted Challenge butter
Then, add mushrooms and toss to coat in butter. - mushrooms - 1 ½ tbsp salted Challenge butter
Cover and let the mushrooms steam for 3-5 minutes. - mushrooms - 1 ½ tbsp salted Challenge butter
Remove the lid and continue to cook, tossing until the liquid evaporates and the mushrooms are golden brown and fragrant. - 1 ½ tbsp salted Challenge butter - mushrooms
Then add thyme. - 1 tsp thyme finely chopped
Keep warm and set aside for serving. - For the Butter Cooked Mushrooms
For the Pearl Onions
Thoroughly dry the pearl onions with paper towels. - pearl onions
In a nonstick pan over medium heat, melt the salted butter, then add the dried pearl onions tossing to evenly coat in butter. - 1 ½ tbsp salted Challenge butter - pearl onions

Cook until the onions begin to brown, then add beef broth. Cover, then once the onions are just tender, remove the lid and braise on the stove for about 30 minutes and allow the liquid to cook off. - 1 cup beef broth - pearl onions
The final result should be jammy and golden brown onions. Keep warm and set aside until ready to serve. - For the Pearl Onions
For the Buttered Noodles
For the Beurre Monté Sauce
In a stainless steel saucepan, add water and bring it up to a simmer. - 1 tbsp water
Then, reduce heat to low and begin adding salted butter, little pieces at a time and whisking constantly over low heat until all the butter has been incorporated. - 1 ½ tbsp salted Challenge butter
The final result should be the consistency of an alfredo sauce. Set aside until ready to serve.
For the Assembly
Remove coq au vin from the oven and transfer chicken thighs to a plate. - For the Coq au Vin Sauce - For the Chicken
Allow the remaining liquid to reduce by half over high heat until it is a thick, glossy sauce. - For the Coq au Vin Sauce
Meanwhile, place the chicken thighs on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet and transfer to 400°F convection oven for 2-3 minutes for a final crisp. - For the Chicken
Cook the pasta, reserving pasta water to maintain butter emulsion. Strain, then toss in the Beurre Monté Sauce, sprinkle with kosher salt - pasta - kosher salt - For the Beurre Monté Sauce
Remove the Bouquet Garni, pressing liquid through a fine mesh sieve to retain flavor. - Bouquet Garni
Add mushrooms and bacon to the sauce, reserving a handful for garnish. Mix to combine and keep the sauce warm until ready to serve. - mushrooms - For the Bacon - For the Coq au Vin Sauce
When the chicken is done crisping in the oven, return to the sauce. - For the Chicken - For the Coq au Vin Sauce

Finally, plate cooked buttered noodles alongside coq au vin sauce, and chicken. Garnish chicken with pearl onions, mushrooms, bacon, and parsley, and the pasta with freshly chopped chives. - Buttered Noodles - Coq au Vin Sauce - Chicken thighs - Pearl Onions - Butter Cooked Mushrooms - Bacon - parsley to garnish - freshly chopped chives to garnish
